Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:12: The fourth blemish is "and turn away from you," and this matter may be explained as it is explained at the end of Parashat Noach (76a) concerning the Shechinah - that when a person is blemished, the Shechinah withdraws from him. And so it is said in the Tikkunim (52b), in these words: "and if the soul becomes soiled with sins, or lacks even a single one of those commandments - as the masters of the Mishnah established, 'a transgression extinguishes a commandment' - in the place where the transgression rests and the commandment has withdrawn from it, that limb is blemished, and this is the soul's defect; because of it the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon the soul. This is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 21:18), 'any man who has a defect shall not draw near' - a soul that has a defect in its two hundred forty-eight commandments does not draw near to Him because of it" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:13: In this manner one may explain the verse here: "for the LORD your God walks," and so on. For it is the way of the Shechinah to walk before a person to guard him, as is explained in Parashat Shelach Lecha (166a); and it is the way of a person to walk behind the Shechinah, as it says (Deuteronomy 13:5), "after the LORD your God shall you walk." And when a person causes a blemish, she withdraws from before him and turns to his rear, so that he is left with no protection before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:14: However, what appears from the language brought afterward - "and therefore, 'the nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover,' why? because it is written, 'it is your father's nakedness'" - explains that the blemish reaches Tiferet as well. If so, it appears that this too is alluded to in the verse, just as "an unseemly thing" [ervat davar] was mentioned: namely, "the nakedness of your father's wife" also alludes to "it is your father's nakedness," in the words "and turn away from you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:15: The matter is that when the Shechinah is blemished because of a person's sin, Tiferet withdraws from her, because she is a throne for him, and he does not rest upon an incomplete throne - as is explained in Parashat Vayikra (4b), and likewise in the Tikkunim, concerning "and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went outside" [Genesis 39:12].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:16: Similarly, it is explained in the Tikkunim (146b), in these words: "in this manner the Holy One, blessed be He, drives away the Shechinah and casts her out of His house - this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 50:1), 'and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.' And is it not so that whoever honors her in exile honors the Holy One, blessed be He, and whoever demeans her demeans the Holy One, blessed be He? And therefore (I Samuel 2:30), 'for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who scorn Me shall be lightly esteemed'" - to this point. The reason for this is that the two of them are two aspects of one countenance, and a king without a queen is not [truly] a king, as Rashbi explained (Vayikra 5a): "'great is the LORD and highly praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain' (Psalms 48:2) - it is heard that a king without a queen is not a king, and is not great, and is not praised" - to this point. And so it is likewise explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim 117b): "the disgrace of the Matrona [Queen] is when they demean her place, and this is the disgrace of the Matrona" - to this point. What is meant by "the disgrace of the Matrona is when they demean her place" will be explained, with God's help, in the matter of the blemish of the Throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:17: What is meant by "and turn away from you" is explained by Rashbi (Shelach 165a): "if he is a pious, holy person, who keeps the covenant properly, He places him behind [Him] and He is in front; and if you say, [what of] one who keeps the rear? Behold, greater and more supernal is the protection of one who keeps it [the covenant fully] - and who is he? The supernal righteous one [tzaddik], who enters with abundant love between 'righteous' [tzaddik] and 'righteousness' [tzedek], and is found protected on every side; happy is he who keeps this covenant" - to this point. And further there (166a) it is proven that when a person is righteous, he walks behind the Shechinah, because the Shechinah walks before him to guard him, as it is written (Exodus 23:20), "behold, I send an angel before you, to guard you" - and the person stands at the level of the righteous one, so that he is behind her; and this is [the meaning of] "after the LORD your God shall you walk." And what they said (see the Zohar, on Berachot 61a), "a man should not walk behind a woman" - the meaning is that he should not descend below into the world of the female, as with Abraham, of whom it is said (Genesis 17:1), "walk before Me" - and it is explained there that this was because he had neither circumcision nor the uncovering [of the corona], and this is a deficiency; for [of Saul, similarly] "he has turned back from following Me" (I Samuel 15:11) means that he descended from the level of the male; and this is what is said there: "he was not behind, because he was not uncovered" - see there. With this we may understand "and turn away from you": that the male, who walks behind you to guard you, withdraws from you because you caused the blemishing of his female counterpart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:18: We may also say that "achareicha" [behind you/after you] refers to the Shechinah, who is called "achor" [rear], as it says (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back [achorai]" - and Tiferet turns away from her because of the blemish. But the first explanation appears to me the primary one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:19: However, one may combine both explanations as one, and say: certainly it is never possible to separate the [divine] unity; for although it is said (Deuteronomy 23:15), "the LORD your God" - this is the Shechinah (in the Zohar mentioned, 75a) - Tiferet is present there as well, as it says, "the LORD, He is God" (ibid. 4:35). Therefore it says, "for the LORD your God walks," and so on - both together, in unity, walk, and so on; and therefore it says, "to deliver you and to give up your enemies," and so on - a double protection corresponding to both of them. And it is explained above that she is called "the guarding of the way," and Tiferet comes to guard her, as it says (Isaiah 42:8), "I am the LORD, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another." And since he comes to guard her, his face is toward her back, in the manner of a guard who follows from behind; and Israel is in between, as it says, "whoever keeps the covenant enters between 'righteous' and 'righteousness.'" And what is meant by "his face is toward her back" is the face of mercy and good providence, to bestow flow upon her - for "back" [achor] indicates withdrawal and concealment; the proof is Adam and Eve, who, when they were back to back, there was no union. Here, in the matter of guarding, there is no union but rather a manner of flow; therefore he was commanded not to blemish the Shechinah, lest he cause the withdrawal of Tiferet from her, and cause Him to turn His face from her, so that they would be back to back - and this is "and turn away from you," stated plainly, referring both to the Shechinah, who is called "back," and to the person, who is in between, whose back is to the male. Thus four aspects of the matter of the blemish have been explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:20: We have seen fit to complete the explanation of this passage, since it bears on our discussion of the blemishing of the Shechinah. It says that for three things Israel is delayed in exile; it says "delayed" because the exile of the Shechinah was decreed for only a thousand years, as it is said (Lamentations 1:13), "He has made me desolate, faint all the day" - and so it is explained in Parashat Va'era (Zohar, Shemot Rabbah context, 17a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:21: The first is "because they treat the Shechinah with contempt in exile" - meaning that they profane the Name of the LORD, as it is said (Ezekiel 36:20), "when they said of them, these are the people of the LORD, yet they have gone out of His land." When Israel does something involving the profanation of the Name, there is no greater disgrace to the Shechinah than this - a parable of a father who has a son, and the son does improper things to people, so that people say, cursed is he who bore this one, cursed is he who raised this one. This applies generally to the whole nation, and in particular to every single individual of Israel who transgresses what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him - he causes disgrace above to the Shechinah, for Scripture says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away." And when a person adds transgression, he adds exile and banishment, for above they say: see the mother, what kind of children she raised! It is fitting, Heaven forfend, that she be banished outside the palace, since she did not discipline her son to be proper - and similarly our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yalkut Bereshit, remez 8, and see remez 27) concerning the nine curses with which the earth was cursed (Tikkunei Zohar 95b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:22: Further, it may be like the matter explained (Tikkunei Zohar 146b): "'honor your father and your mother' - your father, this is the Holy One, blessed be He; your mother, this is the Shechinah. Fear of her is through the negative commandments; honoring her is through the positive commandments - of these it is said, 'for those who honor Me I will honor'; and likewise all those who transgress the negative commandments, of them it is said, 'and those who scorn Me shall be lightly esteemed'" - to the extent relevant here. We find, then, according to this, that the disgrace of the Shechinah is that they do not accord her the honor due to her through the positive commandments, and they transgress the negative commandments. Now, in all matters where a person is obligated in the honor of his earthly father and mother, he is likewise obligated in the honor of the supernal Father and Mother; and just as one is warned not to demean the honor of one's earthly father and mother, and stands under a curse - as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:16), "cursed be he who demeans his father or his mother" - and Rambam wrote (Hilchot Mamrim, chapter 5) that this applies even by a mere gesture - so too one must be careful not to demean the honor of the supernal Father and Mother, and to be careful of everything pertaining to their honor. Of this sort, it appears, one must be careful of what Rashbi said (Terumah 131b; see the Additions 256a), that one who speaks in the synagogue causes disgrace in the supernal arrangement above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:23: The second, "and turn their faces away from the Shechinah," has a general aspect and a particular aspect. The general aspect is like [the actions of] the wicked, who turn back and turn their faces away from the Shechinah, saying with their mouths that they do not wish to have any portion in the God of Israel. The particular aspect is one who breaks off from words of Torah for idle matters, because one who occupies himself with Torah has his face toward the Shechinah, as our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 18; see Tamid 32b), on the verse (Lamentations 2:19), "pour out your heart like water before the presence of the LORD" - and he breaks off; he is found to have turned his face away from the Shechinah. Similarly, one who prays and breaks off in the middle, even if it is during the [Psalms of] praise, and especially if it is during the silent Amidah, and in the middle of his prayer turns his face to look here and there for his own needs - certainly this touches upon the honor of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:24: The third, "and they defile themselves before the Shechinah" - one must be careful in this regard of everything the Torah explicitly calls impurity: the impurity of forbidden foods, as it is said (Leviticus 11:43), "do not make yourselves detestable with any swarming thing that swarms, and do not defile yourselves with them, lest you become defiled through them"; the impurity of forbidden relations (ibid. 18:24), "do not defile yourselves with any of these things, for the nations that I am casting out before you defiled themselves with all these things," and so on; and one must be careful of the impurity of menstrual separation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:25: The impurity of leprous plagues [tzara'at] - our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that plagues come as a result of the sin of slander (Arachin 16a). And Rashbi explained (Metzora 53a): "Rabbi Chiya said: whoever utters slander, all his limbs become defiled," and so on. And in Parashat Shemini (41a) he said: "a person should not blemish his mouth and his tongue, and how much more so should he not defile his own soul and body, for he becomes defiled thereby in the other world" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:26: Also, the impurity of idolatry, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26), "you shall utterly detest it, and utterly abhor it." What bears on this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tetzaveh 182a) - and I shall cite his words below - that one who is angry defiles himself, within and without, like idolatry itself; and of one who is angry it is said (Exodus 34:17), "you shall not make for yourself molten gods" - meaning that he literally makes himself into idolatry. And likewise one who is haughty, and similarly, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Mechilta, Parashat Yitro), on the verse (Exodus 20:18), "and Moses drew near to the thick darkness" - in these words: "and whoever is haughty of heart causes the defilement of the land and the withdrawal of the Shechinah, as it is said (Psalms 101:5), 'one who has a haughty eye and a proud heart, him I cannot endure'; and all who are haughty of heart are called an abomination, as it is said (Proverbs 16:5), 'every haughty heart is an abomination to the LORD.' Idolatry is called an abomination, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26), 'and you shall not bring an abomination into your house' - just as idolatry defiles the land and causes the Shechinah to withdraw," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:27: Also, one must be careful of the impurity of emitting seed in vain, for this sin blemishes the Shechinah, and therefore it says "before the Shechinah." And Rashbi explained (Vayeshev 188a) that there is no sin by which a person defiles himself more than one who emits seed in vain, in these words: "come and see - of all the sins by which a person defiles himself in this world, this is the sin by which a person is defiled the most, in this world and in the World to Come: one who spills his seed uselessly, and emits seed in vain, by hand or by foot, and defiles himself through it - as it is written (Psalms 5:5), 'for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You.' Therefore, he does not enter behind the curtain and does not see the countenance of the Ancient of Days, as we have learned. Here it is written 'evil shall not sojourn with You,' and it is written (Genesis 38:7), 'and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD'; and therefore it is written (Isaiah 1:15), 'your hands are full of blood.' Happy is the portion of the person who fears his Master and keeps himself from the evil way, and purifies himself to occupy himself with the fear of his Master" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:28: There is yet another impurity, although the Torah does not explicitly call it impurity, and it is one who has relations with his wife not in the natural manner; and the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (259a), is stringent about this, in these words: "concerning this we have learned: whoever has relations with his bed from the rear weakens the arrangement of face-to-face gazing, which is meant to illuminate everything together and for everything to be found face-to-face, in fitting union - as it is said (Genesis 2:24), 'and he shall cleave to his wife' - to his wife specifically, and not to the back of his wife" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:29: In these three matters, the word "Shechinah" is mentioned in each and every one, because she is called "Shechinah" [dwelling] on account of her dwelling among the lower beings, specifically among Israel, as it says (Exodus 34:9), "let my Lord, please, go in our midst" - and as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (see Berachot 7a): he asked that the Shechinah rest upon Israel and not upon the idolatrous nations, and the Holy One, blessed be He, agreed. Whoever transgresses one of these matters, behold, the Shechinah is against him and he has no shame of face, and he causes the prolonging of the exile - for Israel was not exiled until they said, "we have no portion in David... every man to his tents, O Israel" (see II Chronicles 10:16) - do not read "le-ohalecha" [to your tents] but "le-Elohecha" [to your gods] (see Yalkut Shmuel, remez 106; Tanchuma, Beshalach 16) - and they denied the God of Israel. And one who sins in the matters mentioned is like one who denies [divine] providence, and was not chastised in exile in proportion to being the cause of the exile; therefore it is fitting, Heaven forfend, that he should be further delayed in exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:30: Let us return to the discourse we began at the start of the chapter, that one must fear not to blemish the Shechinah - this being the "unseemly thing" we explained. There are yet two more aspects concerning the blemish to her, explained in the Tikkunim and in Ra'aya Meheimna.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:31: In the Tikkunim (49b) it is said that the heart is the Shechinah, and there are two chambers in the heart, one the dwelling of the good inclination and the other the dwelling of the evil inclination; and it says that the good inclination is the Shechinah, in the aspects we shall explain, in these words: "'the heart understands, the heart knows, the heart sees' - this is the Shechinah, who takes only what is pure, which is a clean offering of prayer, without bran and without refuse, and she draws near to her husband, the beauty of all. But the lobe of the liver gives her husband only remnants and refuse - and who is her husband? The spleen - 'another god' [el acher] - and from these remnants taken from her, dark and black spleen-blood is made, and this is the deceitful serpent that seduced Eve, who is the heart, and caused her death. And behold, there are two chambers of the heart - which of them does he seduce? Rather, the one on the left, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:2), 'a fool's heart is to his left,' and of which it is said (ibid. 7:26), 'and I find more bitter than death, the woman.' 'A wise man's heart is to his right' - this is the woman of valor, the crown of her husband, of whom it is said (Proverbs 18:22), 'he who finds a wife finds good' - for she is the good inclination, a person's good fortune, of whom it is said (Ezekiel 44:30), 'to cause a blessing to rest on your house' - 'the blessing of the LORD, it enriches' (Proverbs 10:22) - and of her it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:9), 'enjoy life with the wife whom you love'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:32: The intent that emerges from the totality of his words, without examining his language too closely, is that "heart" used plainly refers to the Shechinah, and she has two chambers: one on the right side, the dwelling of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at; and the other on the left side, for the nursing of the judgment of Gevurah - and it is from the left side that the fool clings to his portion below, for all the external [husks] are found below, on the left side, in the sequence of the levels descending. This is [the meaning of] "a wise man's heart is to his right, and a fool's heart is to his left" - for one who wishes to become wise should go to the right, for it is specifically to his right that wisdom comes to him. And her being the dwelling of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at is alluded to by his bringing three verses: the first, corresponding to Da'at, which is in the middle - "this is the woman of valor, the crown of her husband" - and this is a person's "mazal" [fortune/influx], as is explained in the Tikkunim (99b), in these words: "the supernal Vav, which is the supernal mazal that rises in thought." And corresponding to Binah, it is said, "to cause a blessing to rest on your house; the blessing of the LORD, it enriches" - and it is explained in the Tikkunim (27a) that this is Binah. And corresponding to Chochmah, which is life, it says, "enjoy life with the wife whom you love," for love is on the right. And although above I explained, in the name of Rashbi, that the good inclination in general is on the right - the intent there is the right arm, which comprises three joints, namely Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at, as is explained in the Idra (Naso 142a-b); and one may learn what is unclear from what is made explicit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:33: With this we may understand a second explanation of the passage we cited from Parashat Bereshit concerning fear: "why is it called the fear of the LORD? because it is the Tree of Good and Evil," and so on. With this it is explained, for it is the secret of the heart, the dwelling of the good, which is the right; and evil is the secret of judgment, and evil itself extends downward in the sequence of the descending levels. If a person merits, he cleaves to her in the aspect of her right side, which is the good inclination, in the aspects mentioned; if he does not merit, behold, evil cleaves to him, in the secret of "a fool's heart is to his left."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:34: And one must fear the enticements of his inclination, lest he cleave to the spleen, "another god," which is the serpent, that it should draw near to the heart and cause it death. Similarly, this is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Tzav 28b), in a passage we shall cite below, which says: "the sin-offering [chatat] is the lobe of the liver, which grows heavy upon it with the sin-offerings from the stains of Israel's sins - just as the liver makes heavy the blood, which are the sediments upon the arteries of the heart" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:35: And it is explained in the Tikkunim (133a) that whoever is ruled by his [evil] inclination is completely wicked, in these words: "know, my son, that this is the secret of the transmigration of the evil inclination: there is one who resembles a lion, one who resembles a serpent, and one who resembles a donkey - it changes for all creatures according to their deeds and according to the hour in which they were made. And with all this, happy is the soul that rules over it and rides upon it, like a person riding upon a horse or a donkey; woe to him over whom the serpent rules - this one is called completely wicked; and whoever rules over it is completely righteous, and of him it is said (Isaiah 43:4), 'and I will give a man in your place, a wicked man, a man of iniquity, and peoples in place of your soul' - for when a person rules over his inclination, he thereby rules over all who hate him; but if his inclination rules over him, those who hate him rule over him" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:36: And he says at the end of the passage that when a person rules over his inclination, he thereby rules over his enemies - this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said on (Proverbs 16:7), "when the LORD is pleased with a man's ways, He makes even his enemies be at peace with him" - in these words, in Bereshit Rabbah, cited in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 954), on this verse: "Rabbi Yochanan said, 'his enemies' - this refers to his wife; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, this refers to the evil inclination," and so on; "Rabbi Berachiah said, 'even his enemies' includes the harmful creatures of his house, such as fleas, gnats, and flies."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:37: The reason for all this is that when a person strengthens the good inclination over the evil inclination, judgment is thereby subdued beneath mercy; and when the root of the supernal judgment [Gevurah] is sweetened, all the lower branches that flow from the root of Gevurah are all turned to mercy - and this is [the meaning of] "when the LORD is pleased with a man's ways" - that the secret of [divine] favor [ratzon] is bestowed upon "a man's ways," which is Ze'ir Anpin - "the LORD is a man of war" (Exodus 15:3; Zohar I 60a) - and there is the source of judgment (see Zohar III 142b) - "He makes even his enemies be at peace with him," as I have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:38: It is impossible for a person to attain this degree unless he repents with complete repentance and subdues his inclination to the utmost degree of subjugation, and subdues the attribute of judgment within himself, as I explained in the previous chapter; and through this he causes the drawing forth of the flow of [divine] favor to subdue all the masters of judgment who accuse him - as is explained in the Idra, Naso (129a), that at the revelation of the forehead of favor, all wraths are stilled, and these are called "enemies" above. When a person subdues judgment, he causes the drawing forth of the flow of favor to still the lower judgments in this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:39: Further, concerning the matter of the blemish a person causes to the Shechinah, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Tzav 28a-b): they say there that the wings of the dove are the positive commandments, through which she flies upward; and afterward it says, the negative commandments are her captivity, like birds caught in a snare, and all her captivities that prevent her from flying are called adhesions [sirchot] - just as adhesions prevent the wings of the lung from being blown clear, so the guilt-offering [asham] of Israel takes hold of the wings of the Shechinah, which are the Chayot of the Throne, so that she cannot rise up through Israel's merits to the Holy One, blessed be He; and their sins and guilt weigh down and burden her wings, and the guilt-offering [asham] is the mother of the mixed multitude [erev rav]. An adhesion clings to the Throne where the Matrona [Queen] is, and does not allow her to rise up from exile, while merits take hold of her to raise her up; she remains in the air, like an adhesion suspended in the air - and this is the middle pillar, which is the air. So the guilt-offering [asham] is suspended [talui] upon the righteous one [tzaddik], who is suspended between heaven and earth. The sin-offering [chatat] is the lobe of the liver, which grows heavy upon it with the sin-offerings from the stains of Israel's sins, just as the liver makes heavy the blood, which are the sediments upon the arteries of the heart; so these sin-offerings weigh down upon the wings of the Shechinah, which are the positive commandments, resembling the wings of a dove. The negative commandments, when they weigh down upon the positive commandments - that is, when Israel's transgressions are more numerous than their merits - it is said of the Torah, which is the body (Daniel 8:12), "and it cast truth to the ground," and she cries out, "the LORD has given me into hands from which I am unable to rise" (Lamentations 1:14), and "she has fallen, she shall no more rise" (Amos 5:2). And for this reason the Tannaim and Amoraim instituted prayers in the place of the sacrifices, to remove sin-offerings and guilt-offerings from her" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:40: It is explained in this passage that there are two aspects to the matter of the blemish: the first is the blemish of the Shechinah, which is what is said at the end of the passage, that these sins weigh down upon the wings of the Shechinah, which are the positive commandments. And there is also the blemish that reaches Tiferet, "and it cast truth to the ground" - this will be explained further concerning the blemish that reaches Him. And the Shechinah cries out, "the LORD has given me into hands from which I am unable to rise." Therefore one must fear his deeds, and not cause, through his deeds, the outcry of the Shechinah against him and her falling to the ground, as it is written (Amos 5:2), "she has fallen, she shall no more rise."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:41: Further, the matter of the blemish of the Throne is explained in this passage, as it says that the adhesions take hold of the Chayot of the Throne and of the Throne itself, and the Shechinah is clothed in the Throne; and when there is an adhesion there, she does not rise up through the merits of Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:42: Thus the root of fear has been explained in this chapter, an additional explanation of what is said in Parashat Bereshit: "why is it called the fear of the LORD? because it is the Tree of Good and Evil." And everything beneath it is called the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, for it is said in Ra'aya Meheimna (the passage mentioned, Tzav 28b) that an adhesion takes hold of the Throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:43: Close to this aspect of fear in Parashat Bereshit, it is explained in the Tikkunim (77a), in these words: "there is [good] fear and there is [evil] fear: 'the fear of the LORD' - this is the Shechinah, the holy kingship [Malchut]; 'evil fear' - this is a lash to punish the wicked, and what is it? The deadly poison of Samael, his female counterpart. 'The fear of the LORD' is a reward for one who keeps the negative commandments; 'evil fear' is a lash to punish one who transgresses them" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:44: Our intent is explained in his saying, "'the fear of the LORD' is a reward for one who keeps the negative commandments" - for this is the essence of fear: not to transgress a negative commandment and thereby give room to the external forces to blemish and breach the fence to enter within - beyond the several aspects already explained and to be explained further, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:1: Since our explanation in the previous chapter preceded us regarding the root of fear, and we said that it is for a person to distance himself from the evil inclination and draw near to the good, we have seen fit to append this chapter to explain that one should not ignore the enticements of his inclination but overcome it, so that he may be called a mighty one who conquers his inclination - and this is one of the aspects of fear, for we find fear in Gevurah as well as in Binah. Fear in Gevurah is explained in the Tikkunim (10b): that Malchut is called "the fear of the LORD" from the side of Gevurah, and "love" from the side of Chesed. And in Tikkun 2-3 (18b) fear in Binah is explicitly explained, and it says that concerning this it is said (Avot 3:17), "if there is no fear, there is no wisdom."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:2: The matter is as I explained in the previous chapter: one must always fear not to arouse the [evil] inclination and judgment, and the inclination flows from the root of the supernal judgment of these two attributes [Gevurah and Malchut], as Rashbi explained (Noach 70b), on the verse (Genesis 8:21), "I will not again [curse the ground]" - for from these two attributes the root of judgment comes. And a person's overcoming his inclination derives from Gevurah, and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadashim 10a): "in the fifth month He gives strength in Gevurah to overcome the evil inclination from the side of Samael, so that it does not rule over him," and so on - and there the discussion concerns the explanation of the nine months of gestation for the soul of our righteous Messiah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:3: Further, in the Tikkunim (1b), in the explanation concerning six degrees, it says there are pious ones, mighty ones, masters of Torah, and so on, and it says: "mighty ones, from the side of Gevurah, who give strength to their masters to subdue servant beneath master and maidservant beneath mistress through the binding of tefillin" - to this point. Thus, from the side of Gevurah, those who conquer their inclination are called "mighty ones" [giborim] - and this is the reality of fear: to always fear lest the servant [the evil inclination] be let loose and breach the fence, rather than being bound and subdued beneath its master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:4: This matter is further explained in the Zohar (Vayeshev 189b), on the verse (Psalms 103:20), "bless the LORD, His angels, mighty in strength," and so on, [explaining] how much a person must overcome his inclination every single day, in these words: "Rabbi Chiya opened and said, 'bless the LORD, His angels, mighty in strength,' and so on. Come and see how much a person must guard himself from his sins and walk in a proper way, so that the evil inclination, which accuses him every single day, as has been said, should not divert him; and because it accuses him constantly, a person must strengthen himself against it and rise above it into a place of strength, for he must be mightier than it and join himself to the place of Gevurah - for when a person strengthens himself against it, he is then on the side of Gevurah and cleaves to it to strengthen himself; and because that evil inclination is mighty, a person must be mightier than it. And these people who strengthen themselves against it are called 'mighty in strength,' matching its kind with its kind; and these are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, who come from the harsh side of Gevurah to strengthen themselves against it - 'mighty in strength, who do His bidding'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:5: And when it says "he is then on the side of Gevurah and cleaves to it to strengthen himself," this is to indicate what is being taught - that being called a mighty one who conquers his inclination is from the side of Gevurah. And Scripture adds by saying "mighty in strength," for one's strength must be greater than the strength of the evil inclination - this is what is meant by "he must be mightier than it." And without doubt, that Gevurah overcomes the evil inclination is from the power of Binah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (85b) - that strength is in Binah - although this is not explicitly stated in this passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:6: And when it says "and these are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, who come," and so on - this is because the angels were created on the second day (Sefer HaBahir, section 21), and it is explained in Sefer HaBahir that all the angels were created from the fire of Gevurah (see section 145); we find, then, that the righteous one who conquers his inclination is equal to an angel in this respect.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:7: Even though our Sages, of blessed memory, said in tractate Sukkah, chapter HeChalil (52b): Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, a person's inclination overpowers him every day, as it is said (Psalms 37:32), "the wicked watches for the righteous, and seeks to kill him," and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it is said, "the LORD will not abandon him into his hand," and so on - it appears from this that a person's assistance in overcoming his inclination comes from the Holy One, blessed be He, and what praise, then, is there for the righteous one? But the matter is that always, in all things, an arousal from below must come first, as it is said in the Zohar several times (Emor 108b [110b]), "an arousal from below produces an arousal from above" - and this is the praise of the righteous one, that he begins, and afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him; and this is the nature of the word "help" [ezer] - like a person occupied with a burden who cannot manage it, and his companion comes and helps him.
